extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NIH K (career development) applicants, mentors, and institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reviewing NIH K (career development) award applications, emphasizing evaluation of the applicant's potential, training plan, mentorship, research plan, and institutional commitment. Covers mentored K mechanisms (K01, K08, K23, K99/R00, K24, K25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-focused evaluation (key distinction from R-series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike an R01, where the science drives the evaluation, a K-Award is fundamentally about the applicant — their potential, training needs, and career trajectory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review emphasis is on the individual's readiness and potential for an independent research career rather than primarily on the proposed science. Prepare materials that demonstrate candidate development and trajectory as central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic record and research experience; motivation and commitment to a research career; likelihood that the K award will lead to research independence; capacity to develop required skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document past accomplishments, clear motivation, and evidence that the candidate can acquire necessary skills and progress to independence. Reviewers judge whether the individual is a strong investment for career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan (CDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important element of any K award application. Reviewers evaluate whether the CDP fills knowledge/skill gaps for the candidate, specific courses, workshops, conferences, didactic training, plans for protected research time, logical progression toward research independence, and mentor meetings and structured oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed, tailored CDP (not a perfunctory set of courses and meetings). Include concrete training activities, timeline, how protected research time will be provided, and structured oversight. Applications that relegate the CDP to merely "a perfunctory set of courses and meetings" risk negative reviewer judgment because reviewers then must infer candidate potential from the research plan alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims and Research Strategy; whether it is appropriate for and tailored to the applicant's experience level; should be ambitious but feasible within the K timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a research plan that balances ambition and feasibility given the K award duration and the applicant's training stage. Tailor complexity and scope to be developmental (supporting growth) rather than overly independent-project focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor (and Co-Mentors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentor's career and research supervision record; whether mentor's work and experience are relevant to the proposed Research Plan; track record of training individuals (especially K awardees) for successful independent research careers; mentor's commitment of time and effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mentors' biosketches and evidence of prior trainee success, explicit descriptions of how mentors will support and the time they will commit. Letters and plans should demonstrate a clear, active mentoring role aligned with the CDP and research plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and Institutional Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the institution has suitable facilities; institution's commitment to the applicant's development as an investigator; protected time guarantee (typically 75% effort); departmental support letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include institutional letters that commit protected research time (commonly ~75% effort) and describe resources and programmatic support. Demonstrate that the environment will facilitate training, mentorship, and transition to independence.
